newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi backs idea of moving fast on Italy 98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Prodi backs idea of moving fast on Italy 98 budget.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday he supported the idea of moving approval of Italy's 1998 budget law forward to mid-summer if parliament agreed.
"I think there is every reason for bringing forward the budget because it is useful to the country," Prodi told reporters in response to questions.
He said the step would reassure financial markets of Italy's intent to put its finances in order and he believed it could win opposition backing since it was an issue of common interest.
Feasibility discussions had been held with Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and the Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house), Luciano Violante.
The budget has to be drawn up by September 30 and passed into law by both houses of parliament by December 31.
Prodi was asked about the timetable after Ciampi told Italian reporters in Brussels on Monday that the budget could be approved as early as August 15 if political forces were committed.
He said such a move would be a clear signal that Italy wanted to take part in the the first wave of European Monetary Union (EMU).

Former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, leader of the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance, said Ciampi's proposal should be taken seriously because it would benefit the country but added that he believed it would be very difficult.
